analysis:
The only changed code is SSDPrefixCache.retireIndexedEntries (head ~1794-1800). It previously ran one SSDOwnedEntryRetirement.remove(urls:) call inside a single removalLock.withLock. It now calls SSDOwnedEntryRetirement.removeInSlices(urls) and takes removalLock per slice, running the same remove(urls: slice, ...) body. The hasSafeRoot and ownsEvictionRoot guards are re-evaluated per slice, and a nil result is returned when they fail. The change is related to T-041 (SSD prefix cache at-rest tier), A-001, TB-007 and T-016/availability.

Behavioral concerns checked:
1. The removal barrier (removalLock) is no longer held across the whole batch. Concurrent donate/stage paths could interleave between slices. These paths already tolerate index/file races through forgetMissing, performIndexedRemoval and in-flight tag handling, so the safety margin appears unchanged. Reading block files does not hold removalLock.
2. Whether a nil slice result aborts the remaining slices, and how the results are merged (removed set, indexedBytesFreed, externalChange), depends on removeInSlices. That implementation is not in the supplied evidence. If an early stop or a partial merge drops externalChange, reconcileExternalRemovals could be skipped. That would risk stale index entries or missed TTL/LRU purges, which weakens the T-041 mitigation (b) but is not a confidentiality issue.
3. Safety checks inside remove (no-follow, under-root, epoch store) are unchanged per slice.

No concrete regression is demonstrable from the supplied evidence. Residual question for integration: the removeInSlices semantics (slice size, abort-on-nil, result merging, and the fallback for an empty urls array, which should yield .init()), plus callers such as the TTL sweep and evictOldestEntry that rely on atomic batch retirement.
